chunks: From him, from Faḍālah, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم kissed ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn after his death. Thus, the proper way regarding these two reports is that we interpret them to mean that if the kissing takes place after death, before the body becomes cold, or after the ghusl, then ghusl does not become obligatory because of it, as we have explained in the report of ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān. That report is detailed, while these two reports are general, and judging by the detailed report takes precedence over judging by the general one, and that does not conflict with this.

key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: Does kissing or touching a deceased person require ghusl in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This report states that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم kissed ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn after his death. The ruling derived here is that touching or kissing a deceased person before the body becomes cold, or after the deceased has been given ghusl, does not necessitate ghusl, with the detailed report being preferred over the general one.
